FR-F1: not built: lane capacity is fixed, not earned. The lane pool has a set size (GF_LANES_SIZE, default 3; kernel/lanes.py Lanes) and a project's build runs its tasks one cell at a time (kernel/dispatch.py build). Nothing computes verified progress per euro per lane (contract x phase x work class) over a sliding window, and nothing grows or shrinks a lane's cells. It would take a scheduler that reads the gate verdicts and priced gnomon_run costs already in each ledger, computes yield per lane over a window, and sets the lane's concurrent cells additively up and multiplicatively down, with a build able to run more than one cell at a time.
FR-F2: not built: a product's lanes compile no scout role (kernel/lanes.py writes only builder and verifier, plus the analyst lane's toolless roles), and no lane has a budget, so there is nothing to keep 10% of. The factory's own hand-written .gnomon/roles.toml has a scout for building Rihma itself, but no scheduler places it. It would take per-lane budgets, a compiled read-only scout role, and the FR-F1 scheduler keeping one scout and about a tenth of the budget on every active lane.
FR-F3: partly built: every task a product contract compiles writes the same scope (app/**, tests/**) and depends on the task before it (kernel/compile.py to_contract), and the build loop runs one cell at a time (kernel/dispatch.py build), so a shared write scope never has two cells at once (FR-F3-AC-1, FR-F3-AC-2); not built: the factory never measures how much two tasks' write scopes overlap, so the cap is one cell for every lane, overlapping or not. Telling heavy overlap from disjoint scopes matters only once a scheduler can run several cells in one lane (FR-F1).
FR-F4: not built: Gnomon detects stalls inside a run (stall_signal records, stop reason 'stall'), and the kernel only counts them on ingest. There is no calibrated stall window per cell, no per-cell budget to return, and no recall. The kernel also stops runs on elapsed time, against the requirement's second sentence: build_task passes --deadline 1500 to gnomon, and run_gnomon_task (kernel/model.py) kills the process after deadline + 600 seconds, which is recorded as an apparatus failure. It would take a stall window calibrated from past cells' time to verified progress, a recall that ends the cell and credits its unspent budget back to the lane, and that recall in place of the wall-clock kill.
FR-F6: not built: the decision queue read model (kernel/dashboard.py queue) reports the open decision cards with their count, oldest and median age, but the approval inbox has no work-in-progress limit, no p90 age, no age target, and no lane slows down when approvals pile up. It would take a WIP limit and a p90 age target in the factory's policy, the p90 computed from the open cards' ages, and a check in the spec and build loops that holds back the lanes whose work opens approval cards while the target is passed.
FR-F7: partly built: an escalation Gnomon makes inside a builder cell is recorded against that cell's task and round with the model it ended on (kernel/dispatch.py _cell_summary, the cell_ran event, the task timeline), and the run's tokens and priced cost are ingested against the same task and round (kernel/dispatch.py ingest_latest_run, adapters/gnomon_ingest.py ingest) (FR-F7-AC-1, FR-F7-AC-2); not built: nothing checks a prompt against the local model's window before a cell starts, and a product's lanes compile no escalation policy: kernel/lanes.py gives the builder a cloud primary with a local fallback that Gnomon uses only when an endpoint fails, so 'local first, then cloud only on stall, failed verification or deadline share' exists only in the factory's own hand-written .gnomon/roles.toml ([roles.builder.escalate]). An escalated run is also priced whole at the model it ended on: its local leg's tokens are charged at the cloud price (adapters/gnomon_ingest.py ingest prices record['model'] over all the run's tokens).
